work_order.approach: Apply the v2 fix-forward, which was verified correct but never landed on the branch: three surgical corrections on sdlc/issue-16, one per QA bug, each with a regression test. (1) src/web/pages.js renderPage: derive tenantName from the effective (post-override) state instead of only from the store — when the resolved state is 'empty' the header reads 'No connected account', otherwise it names the first tenant or falls back to 'No connected account'. The page bodies already branch on the effective state and are untouched. (2) src/api/routes.js /v1 catch-all: report request.baseUrl + request.path (the path the client actually called, without query string) instead of mount-relative request.path, so the envelope names /v1/events rather than /events. (3) package.json sdlc:ready: curl http://localhost:${PORT:-3000}/health so the readiness probe follows the same $PORT the server honours, keeping the 3000 default. Add regression coverage: a seeded-DB ?state=empty header/body agreement case in test/web/pages.test.js, a POST /v1/events full-path envelope case in test/api/health.test.js, and a new test/ops/ready-script.test.js asserting the ready script honours $PORT. Then run npm run sdlc:verify green and confirm the diff actually contains the three source edits plus the three test changes before handing back.

work_order.root_cause: The page chrome and the page body answer two different definitions of 'empty'. renderPage resolves the body from the effective (post-override) state but computes the header tenantName solely from the store's first tenant, so ?state=empty on a seeded DB renders an empty body under a 'Demo Tenant' header (BUG-1, user-visible) — directly contradicting docs/ui.md, which defines empty as 'No connected account yet'. The same class of underspecification produced the other two: the /v1 catch-all reports Express's mount-relative request.path instead of the client-called path (BUG-2), and sdlc:ready hardcodes :3000 while the server honours $PORT (BUG-3). None of these touches the ticket's core invariants — all ten original acceptance criteria and all 33 unit tests pass — which is why the slice looked done while three operator- and user-facing inconsistencies shipped with it.

POST /v1/events returns 404 with code NOT_FOUND and a message containing the full path '/v1/events' (fails before the fix, which reports '/events')

work_order.understanding: The previous work order's (v2) diagnosis was RIGHT, not wrong — and I verified that before writing anything else. BUG-1 reproduces live: seeded repositories plus override=empty on /journal yields header 'Demo Tenant' with the empty body and data-state=empty, on all five routes; the QA screenshot of /?state=empty shows the same contradiction directly. BUG-2 (routes.js line 43 uses mount-relative request.path) and BUG-3 (package.json hardcodes :3000) are exactly as v2 described. What the previous attempt got wrong was execution, not diagnosis: branch HEAD adc2939 is byte-identical to the commit QA tested, no commits followed the QA verdict, v2's demanded test/ops/ready-script.test.js does not exist on the branch, and the existing suites lack every v2 regression case. In other words PR #27 as QA saw it was still the v1 implementation — the v2 fix-forward was never built, so there is no evidence against its approach and no failure-packet.json repeat signature. This v3 therefore re-issues the same three surgical fixes with the same regression tests (AC-1..AC-13 carried forward verbatim, none renumbered or dropped), plus a diff check in qa_script so a second no-op handoff cannot pass silently. No criterion is wrong and none changes; stop.json is not warranted (nothing environmental, no forbidden paths, QA and the code agree).
